evidence: The no-pick test guarded only `THEMES[0] !== "nord"` and then indexed `THEMES[i + 1]!` unwrapped, so nord landing last would yield undefined. Commit 488033d adds `themeAt(k)` with the ring's `((k % n) + n) % n` wrap and also replaces the unwrapped `THEMES[i + 1]` in the click and settings-menu tests, which the reviewer had not named.
guidance_note: When a test steps through a cyclic domain, write the index helper with the production wrap once and use it in every test in the block, instead of guarding only the one boundary the fixture happens to hit.

guidance_note: When you write a comment that contradicts a documented contract elsewhere in the repo, fix or ticket the stale doc in the same commit, so the contradiction is not left for a reviewer to find.

evidence: SETTING_PROJECTIONS was introduced in 35e4d2d with a sessionKey column that duplicates settings-menu.ts's control records. In the agent's own review summary it 'Partly declined as out of scope' folding that table, then folded it in 8682896 when the CI reviewer raised the same point. narrative: Round 0 raised one test-robustness finding. Rounds 1 and 2 reviewed 35e4d2d, the agent's batch of fixes from its own local /code-review cycle. That commit caused a real regression (F3: demo style label blank after the `(default)` fallback was removed) and left the duplicate projection table the agent had partly declined to fold (F4). F2 was a reviewer misreading caused by a stale doc in funcs.ts, and the agent refuted it with an engine probe. If the table had been folded in 35e4d2d, round 2 would most likely have approved and round 3 would not have been needed.
guidance_observations: Fix-caused findings came from fixes for local-review findings, which the packet cannot name by id, so the cause fields understate how much of this PR's review cost was self-inflicted.
The agent reproduced F3 before fixing it and found the header's documented command never loaded the file, which turned a template patch into a single-source payload fix.
Declining a duplication as 'pre-existing' after your own diff deepened it cost a full CI round when the CI reviewer raised the same point.
